model_annotation: Figure 4 displays a horizontal bar chart titled “Number of participants (N = 6) who highlighted each evaluation criterion as beneficial.” The chart compares six evaluation criteria along the vertical axis, which are listed in descending order of participant endorsement: “Retrieval of relevant fact-checks (FCs),” “Concise summaries and explanations,” “Clarity of the interface,” “Veracity graph,” “Overall usability,” and “Output quality.” The horizontal axis represents the number of participants, ranging from 0 to 6, with tick marks at intervals of 1. Each criterion is represented by a single horizontal bar, colored in a light gray shade, with the length corresponding to the number of participants who rated it as beneficial. The bar for “Retrieval of relevant fact-checks (FCs)” is the longest, extending to 6, indicating all six participants highlighted it as beneficial. The bars for “Concise summaries and explanations” and “Clarity of the interface” are also full-length, reaching 6. The “Veracity graph” bar reaches 5, while “Overall usability” and “Output quality” both reach 4. The bars are not grouped or stacked, and there are no additional visual annotations or legends. The chart visually emphasizes that the retrieval of relevant fact-checks, concise summaries and explanations, and interface clarity were most highly rated by participants.
